page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.6xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by a dedicated 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8269CY CPU based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 24 vCPUs spread across 12 physical cores with hyperthreading, providing 2 threads per core. The system is provisioned with 48.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB RAM per vCPU consistent with compute-centric infrastructure. Additional hardware features include 35 MB of L3 cache, support for AVX-512 vector instructions with VNNI, AES encryption extensions, and baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps. This instance configuration includes no local NVMe storage drives or GPU hardware.

Benchmark evaluations place the ecs.c6.6xlarge in the average performance tier across multi-threaded computational workloads, achieving a PassMark CPU score of 21,643.62 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 8,967.0. However, single-threaded execution exhibits lower throughput; stress-ng single-core execution (1,313.3) and single-threaded gzip compression (22.86 GB/sec) rank in the bottom 25% of benchmarked hardware. Memory bandwidth scales moderately, reaching 108.94 GB/sec for uncached reads and 47.99 GB/sec for uncached writes. Database handling demonstrates steady output with Redis SET operations recording 20.09 million operations per second and static web serving reaching 15.86 GB/sec throughput.

From a qualitative cost efficiency perspective, the ecs.c6.6xlarge offers balanced multi-core density for workloads requiring parallel processing power without needing high memory ratios or attached local disks. The integration of AVX-512 extensions benefits software compilation (Geekbench compilation score of 17,481.0) and vectorized data processing. Primary trade-offs center on lower single-core processing speeds and reliance on network storage. Recommended workload fits include multi-threaded batch compilation, CI/CD build environments, web serving, ETL data transformation, and distributed in-memory caching.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.6xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on x86_64 architecture with a dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at 2.5 GHz. It provides 24 vCPUs across 12 physical cores, 48.0 GB of system RAM, 35 MB of L3 cache, and 8 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. Built without local storage or GPU accelerators, the instance relies on network-attached storage. Benchmark results show average multi-core processing capability, achieving a PassMark CPU score of 21,643.62 and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression speeds of 101.61 GB/sec, though single-core performance ranks in the lower quartile. The 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation delivers cost-effective density for compute-bound tasks requiring parallel execution. The instance is well suited for software compilation, web serving, multi-threaded data processing, and distributed key-value caching.
